{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.9,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R62"],
      "pins": ["R62.1", "R62.2"],
      "nets": ["+3V3", "Net-(U15-Y)"],
      "observed": "R62 is placed as a pull-up from +3V3 to Net-(U15-Y), but its schematic value is \"10\" and the SPICE deck models it as 10 Ω.",
      "expected": "R62 should be a 10 kΩ pull-up, consistent with its own MPN/description/LCSC data and with the neighboring pull-up resistors R61 and R63.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R62\") (value \"10\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 100mW Thick Film Resistors 75V ±100ppm/℃ ±1% 10kΩ 0603 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \" 0603WAF1002T5E\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"165\") (name \"Net-(U15-Y)\") ... (node (ref \"R62\") (pin \"2\") ..."},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R62 +3V3 Net-_U15-Y_ 10"}
      ],
      "impact": "A 10 Ω pull-up is three orders of magnitude too low for this node. When U15 pulls Net-(U15-Y) low, the resistor would dissipate roughly 1 W and demand hundreds of mA from +3V3, exceeding the 0603 resistor rating and likely overwhelming the buffer output. This would distort the e-stop/LED indicator logic and could damage the board.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The design files show a clear wrong-value anomaly: R62 is modeled as 10 Ω in a +3V3 pull-up position, while its component metadata and circuit role indicate 10 kΩ. This would make the board behave differently from the intended design and is the most defensible finding."
}
